question: A fintech company needs to run a nightly review of several million archived transaction documents. The job can tolerate hours of turnaround, but the finance team wants to minimize per-document processing cost as much as possible. Which two features should the architecture combine?
options: A) Extended thinking, since exposing the full reasoning trace for each document is required to justify the review's cost savings.
B) Prompt caching, since the shared review instructions and reference criteria can be cached across the millions of documents.
C) Computer use, since taking screenshots of each document lets Claude review content it cannot otherwise access.
D) Batch processing, since asynchronous batch requests cost 50% less than standard synchronous API calls.
E) Fast mode, since delivering higher output speed at premium pricing is the most direct way to lower the cost of the nightly run.
correct_answers: B) Prompt caching, since the shared review instructions and reference criteria can be cached across the millions of documents.
D) Batch processing, since asynchronous batch requests cost 50% less than standard synchronous API calls.
explanations: Incorrect. Extended thinking adds reasoning tokens and cost per document; it is not needed to justify cost savings and works against the goal of minimizing per-document cost.
Correct. Prompt caching lets the shared review instructions and criteria be reused across millions of documents, cutting reprocessing cost on top of batch discounts.
Incorrect. Computer use is for controlling computer interfaces via screenshots and input commands; archived transaction documents don't require screen-based interaction to be reviewed.
Correct. Batch processing is designed for exactly this scenario: asynchronous, latency-tolerant, high-volume workloads that cost 50% less than standard synchronous calls.
Incorrect. Fast mode trades premium pricing for higher output speed, which raises cost per request rather than lowering it, and speed is not the priority for an overnight, latency-tolerant job.
